summary:
I shipped "Talk to Virtual Me" on phillipsben.com — a career assistant that answers questions about my work using only what's published on the site. No vector database: the whole knowledge base is around 12k tokens, so it fits in-context. A build-time redaction guard assembles the knowledge pack at compile time and strips confidential material before the model ever sees it, making leaks structurally impossible rather than prompt-engineered around. I ran a 16/16 adversarial battery before shipping — fabrication attempts, prompt injection, open-relay probes. The backend choice was a deliberate trade: I benchmarked cold prefill on the local P100 (around 10 seconds warm, up to 48 seconds cold after eviction by another service) and defaulted to Claude Haiku for responsiveness, keeping local as an opt-in.

For phillipsben.com's project pages I've been generating abstract SDXL hero images and duotoning them to the site palette. The prompt-craft work on the Pascal-era P100 took some iteration: line-centric prompts reliably drift into generic flowing curves on this checkpoint, so dot-field and stipple compositions work far better. Concrete nouns cause other problems — "message bus" prompted a literal coach bus, "bounded frame" a picture hanging on a wall. Most concepts needed three or four seeds and reworded prompts. Separately, I built a ComfyUI custom node that acquires a GPU lease from Switchboard before a render starts, so image generation workflows now queue alongside the 26B language model instead of competing for VRAM.

BudgetTracker has seven years of bank transactions in it, and a large share of the dollar figures were money movement rather than actual spending — Zelle transfers, brokerage contributions, car financing — sitting in the income and expense buckets and making the totals useless. I built a transfer-detection service that identifies these by merchant and description pattern and re-tags them, then ran it over the history. The net income figure went from a number that reflected nothing real to one that reads as actual spending against earnings across those years. On the AI side, I wired the insights layer to the local 26B model via Switchboard, which required handling its reasoning output — it splits responses into a thinking block and actual content, and short-budget utility calls were returning empty content until I added a flag to disable thinking on those.

I repurposed an ESP32-S3 into the Rep Counter — an on-device barbell rep counter that tracks a color-coded plate as a fiducial, with no server or ML involved. The detection runs on raw RGB565 directly from the camera; decoding to JPEG and back gave unreliable results, which I only confirmed after trying three different decode paths. It counted 5/5 reps in a dim living room on first real test. On the home-automation side: when my phone enters a store's geofence, a webhook fires and sends a Telegram voice note with the TickTick shopping list for that store and my checking balance from BudgetTracker. The spoken balance has to be spelled out as words — the TTS reads raw digits like a year, so "$7,032" comes out "seventy thirty-two."

highlights.oneLiner: Shipping 'Talk to Virtual Me' career assistant + SDXL hero image generation for project pages
Transfer detection pass to re-tag 7 years of money-movement; wiring AI layer to local 26B via Switchboard
ComfyUI GPU-coordinator custom node; P100 serialization now covers image gen workflows
On-device barbell rep counter on ESP32-S3 using raw RGB565 color-plate tracking, no ML
